A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TableRAG and HeteQA. The complete main text and appendices are readable, and retained equations, experiments, figures, and prompts can be matched despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Table 1, component ablations, execution and error analyses, and appendix sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds latency measurements, exact-match results, and supplementary baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The offline databases, four-stage retrieval/SQL reasoning loop, and operational prompts are unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds implementation explanations; its SQL-error fallback was already specified in v1's intermediate-answer prompt.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HybridQA, WikiTQ, and the same 304-example HeteQA benchmark. The added evaluations reuse this coverage without introducing new datasets, domains, or task scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D.2 adds TAP4LLM on HybridQA and H-Star on WikiTQ, using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct in Table 5. The original Table 1 comparator lineup remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 substantially broadens measurement beyond the retained LLM-judge accuracy and iteration counts: Appendix D.1 adds exact-match evaluation across all three datasets, and Section 6.2 measures total and per-step latency on WikiTQ and HeteQA. Existing retrieval settings, chunk sizes, and iteration limits are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, error and domain analyses, top-k sensitivity study, and worked HeteQA example are retained. v1 Appendix D's analyses move to v2 Appendix E; the new result tables introduce no additional ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added latency and exact-match tables provide point results without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 scores and plotted results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 2, 4, and 5. Under the newly reported exact-match metric, DeepSeek-V3 TableRAG scores 33.1 versus ReAct's 35.4 on HybridQA. Table 2 reports higher total latency for TableRAG: 17.70 versus 13.50 seconds on WikiTQ and 45.65 versus 24.57 on HeteQA. These are additional evaluations, not changes to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The task formulation and mathematical definitions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: SQL-assisted heterogeneous reasoning, HeteQA, and claimed superiority over existing approaches. Replacing 'hybrid' with 'SQL-based' restates the already-described method.

C2.justification: v2 adds a latency explanation attributing claimed speed advantages to SQL execution and fewer iterations, although Table 2 reports the opposite latency ordering. Appendix D.2 also infers a general advantage of agentic frameworks over pipelines from the added comparison. The explicit limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.3 documents missing-value handling, column-type inference, and representative-value selection during preprocessing. v2 also supplies implementation links for the added baselines. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish changes to the original experimental settings.

R1.justification: Appendix D.2 introduces descriptions of TAP4LLM and H-Star and positions TableRAG against their processing strategies. The main related-work section and bibliography remain unchanged; the added methods have repository footnotes but unresolved citation markers.

P1.justification: v2 revises the author header, standardizes the SQL-based description, and clarifies the explanation of query over-decomposition. It subdivides the efficiency section, adds an experiments appendix, and removes the obsolete Prompt Design subsection with its broken reference. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds latency, exact-match, and supplementary-baseline tables and clarifies Table 1's metric caption. The existing HeteQA example moves from Table 2 to Table 3, while figures retain their content despite relocation. Layout changes also leave the prompts heading on a nearly empty page.

improvement.justification: The added exact-match results, targeted baselines, and preprocessing details improve empirical coverage and transparency. However, new Section 6.2 claims lower latency while Table 2 consistently reports higher latency, including 45.65 versus 24.57 seconds on HeteQA. Table 4 also introduces an exception to the retained broad superiority claim without discussing it. The PDFs cannot resolve whether the timing table or its interpretation is wrong, leaving useful additions alongside substantive inconsistencies and no reliably assessable net improvement.
